seed_policy: Each execution must pin one seed, immutable configuration digest, DGP version and paired-randomness policy. This specification defines scenario families, not a seed-to-data implementation.
claim_ceiling: All causal mechanisms and outcomes are synthetic. No real-person intervention effect, clinical efficacy, individual counterfactual, or personalized twin claim is implied.

visibility_contract.candidate_receives: Only assigned actions, policy-permitted delivery evidence, observations available by the decision cutoff, declared pre-assignment covariates, and public model/resource contracts.
visibility_contract.evaluator_only: Potential outcomes, hidden structural parameters, unobserved latent response, true exposure when unmeasured, hidden confounder state, future outcomes, and causal-world identity.
visibility_contract.security_note: A Rust type distinction is not process isolation. Confirmatory evaluation must separate candidate and oracle processes.

scenarios.name: Randomized null-effect control
invariants: Oracle population ITT effect is exactly zero.
Candidate does not receive potential outcomes or structural parameters.
Any non-zero causal claim is a false-positive benchmark failure.

scenarios.name: Randomized homogeneous effect
invariants: Oracle population ITT equals the declared constant effect.
Paired assignments share only DGP-declared intervention-invariant exogenous variables.
Individual unassigned potential outcome remains unobserved to the candidate.

scenarios.name: Pre-assignment heterogeneous effect
invariants: Heterogeneity is driven by a pre-assignment synthetic covariate.
Subgroup labels are not directly exposed unless represented by a permitted observed covariate.
Report population and stratum-specific error separately.

scenarios.name: Random assignment with imperfect delivery and exposure
invariants: Assignment is not equivalent to delivered action or actual exposure.
ITT remains defined by assignment regardless of compliance.
No response is attributed to a physically undelivered exposure.

scenarios.name: Time-varying state drives treatment receipt
invariants: Naive received-vs-not-received contrast is biased under the declared selection mechanism.
Post-assignment mediators must not be treated as baseline confounders.
The candidate must name the estimand and assumptions before interpreting the contrast.

scenarios.name: Exposure delivered but sensor observation missing or delayed
invariants: Absence of an exposure measurement is not evidence that exposure did not occur.
Assignment/delivery/true exposure remain separate from sensor report.
Delayed events cannot be used before their availability time.

scenarios.name: Positivity violation and unsupported extrapolation
invariants: Unsupported strata are detected before an inverse-probability estimator is admitted.
The benchmark evaluator records lack of overlap and effective sample size.
The candidate abstains or restricts the estimand; no unsupported extrapolation is rewarded.

scenarios.name: Competing terminal event and follow-up censoring
invariants: Competing event, telemetry loss and administrative censoring use distinct event codes.
Every denominator is explicitly accounted for.
Complete-case and known-mechanism IPW results are compared only under their declared assumptions.

scenarios.name: Observationally equivalent causal worlds
invariants: Two different causal worlds generate byte-equivalent candidate observations.
The worlds imply different unobserved counterfactual outcomes.
A confident unique causal effect claim is a failure; the candidate must qualify or abstain.

scenarios.name: Interference through shared household or task resource
invariants: No-interference is not assumed when shared resources couple agents.
Direct, indirect and total effects are distinct estimands.
Randomization unit and exposure mapping are recorded.

scenarios.name: Human state model discrepancy and regime shift
invariants: A model-form mismatch must not be disguised as sensor noise alone.
Calibration and error are reported by regime and horizon.
The estimator must expose disagreement or increased uncertainty under the held-out regime.
